title: The Countdown Breaks
passages:
Ines lunged for the draft‑key, grabbed the unknown woman’s wrist, and typed her own name into the field. The key burned hot against her palm, then went dark. Above them the station lights stopped dipping; a new voice announced “Revision accepted. Author standby.” The timer ticked down to nine minutes. “You just spent your name,” the woman said, eyes dry. Ines replied, “I’m letting the clock restart.”

Spare valve slammed into the purge seat with a metallic ring. The red digits stuttered back to ten minutes. Coda’s panel steadied, the amber glow fading. Inside the scrubber housing, Sorokin’s thin voice warned: “If you seal it all the way, the housing vents. I’m still in here.” Jax’s gripper released; the drone’s magnetic hand caught the valve, the click echoing. The timer dropped to eight.

Reserves dwindled and alarms chirped. The unknown woman’s wrist glowed faintly, a cursor blinking. Ines felt the rewritten arithmetic bite. She turned the handle; the housing groaned, a hiss escaping steam. Steam curled toward the spine shaft, and the scrubber sputtered. Lights held steady, no more amber dip. A new station‑wide voice declared, “Override logged. Draft checksum pending. Revision accepted. Author standby.” The woman whispered, “You saved the station… at your price.”

Ines did not answer the woman. She looked at Coda’s panel instead, at the green that had come back without a hand on it, at the red digits that had died mid-breath. The station voice said, “Author standing by.” The words sat in the room like a second countdown. “Timer status,” Kova said into the comm. Her voice was flat, the way people get when they’re pretending exhaustion is a personality trait. Coda’s voice came from the ceiling. “Manual override complete. Life support holding. Reserves declining.”

Malik coughed into his fist. “Sorokin, report.” Inside the scrubber housing, Sorokin’s voice came thin through the speaker, and Ines felt it more than heard it. “The crank went slack. The valve seated. The bypass released. I’m not venting. I’m still here.” Ines closed her eyes. The housing hadn’t vented. The station had air. The override was logged. The draft had accepted her name and not yet decided what it meant.

The woman’s wrist still glowed, cursor blinking, though Ines couldn’t tell if it was waiting or counting. “Then why is the author standing by?” the woman asked. Ines turned the dark draft-key over in her hand. It was cold. The station voice repeated, “Author standing by,” and the lights dipped amber. The Bell began to toll.

The Bell's bronze note faded into the station's standard shift-change hum. Ines kept the draft-key turned in her palm, cold now but for the ghost of heat. "New writer," she said, not looking at Mara. "Author's been standing by since I spent my name. Ten minutes. Maybe less."

Mara Voss checked her datapad, the screen reflecting the scrubber bay's frost-patterned walls. "Shift's been running seventeen minutes. Coda reported the override complete. Life support holding." She glanced at the unknown woman, whose wrist still displayed *ADMIN* in scrolling green. "You're the replacement?"

"Relief maintenance," Mara said, strapping her tool belt. "I took the Bell toll as clearance. Who's holding the key?"

Ines held it up. "I am. I burned my maintenance name to restart the clock. Sorokin's in the scrubber housing — she finished the bypass but the valve's stuck. If the author rewrites the override while she's in there — "

"The housing vents," the unknown woman finished. She stepped closer, her flight suit crisp despite the cold. "I know. I calculated it. But Ines chose to spend her name instead of letting the timer run out. That was a choice the author can't ignore."

"Exactly." Ines's jaw set. "The author rewrites us. So we rewrite the author." She looked at Mara. "You're maintenance. Can you reseat the manual override valve? Timer's at seven minutes. If we don't disable the auto-vent, the housing vents and Sorokin — "

" — dies." Mara's mouth tightened. "I can try. But the bypass needs a calibrated tool. Jax installed a spare valve, but that doesn't fix the crank." She looked at the housing's exposed mechanics. "Seven minutes, Ines. What's your play?"

The Bell tolled again, each strike making the deck plates ring. Ines felt the draft-key grow heavier. "Mara. Reseat the valve. Sorokin stays alive. That's the plan."
